back: A single natural feature of the Earth's surface with a recognisable shape, e.g. a hill, valley, plateau or escarpment.
The whole scene of an area: several landforms together with vegetation, rivers and human features.
The differences in height and the shape (flat, gentle, steep) of the land surface in an area.
A long steep slope separating higher land from lower land, e.g. the Zambezi escarpment.
An isolated, steep-sided hill of hard rock rising abruptly from a plain ('island mountain').
Mount Nyangani, about 2,590 m (Eastern Highlands); the Runde-Save confluence, about 160 m (south-east lowveld).
Highveld (above about 1,200 m), middleveld (about 900-1,200 m), lowveld (below about 900 m) and the Eastern Highlands.
A ridge of high ground running roughly SW-NE through Bulawayo, Gweru and Harare, dividing rivers flowing to the Zambezi from those flowing to the Limpopo and Save.
Farmland and towns (plateaus), dam sites (gorges), plantations and tourism (highlands), stone and heritage sites (hills), fertile soils (flood plains).
